claim_one_line: THE WEAVE'S ANOMALY, VERIFIED ON MAIN (re-banks the SM seat's W101; rule 12ffb5421 before script ac37cbc8b before run b1f77ade9; re-run byte-identical; every claim checked with main's independent code): det rho = chi_eta^9 (t-exponents 1/8, 3/8, 7/8; s and 200 words agree; image order 96). If the moves act on the fermions as a symmetry: the mixed anomaly with SU(3) vanishes exactly when s_u = s_d = -s_Q (16 of 64, the moves acting on left- and right-handed quarks alike); with SU(2) never (n in {6, 12, 18}; binding only if gauged); with gravity, given SU(3)-freedom, exactly when s_e = s_nu = -s_L, never without nu^c. det(Y_u Y_d) carries chi_eta^m, m = -9(2s_Q + s_u + s_d), and is eta^(6K) times a modular function iff 6K = m (mod 24); det Y_1 = 8 eta^6; with real coefficients and no counterterm theta-bar - theta = -12 arg eta (mod pi), pi/2 on Re tau = 1/2; at weights 3 (all in T) and 2 (vectorial) the determinants are eta^6 E_6 and E_6 times constants, and with the counterterm g is a constant times j - 1728. The control C1 failed as worded (a principal branch of q^(1/4)); repaired post hoc and disclosed. 0 of 19.
